content: xixi-box removed the review request for wasmtime-compiler-reviewers from PR #15285.

xixi-box opened PR #15285 from xixi-box:fix/issue-15277-5d042ce-c9d671a3 to bytecodealliance:main:

Fixes #15277

Root cause: A call return PC can equal the following interrupt_poll fault PC, causing distinct user stack maps to share an address and violate their strict ordering; inserting a NOP before the poll when these PCs collide preserves both maps.

<!-- oss-scout-job:job-9193e006-1300-423c-9dd2-c9d671a305f3 -->

Tests: target/debug/clif-util test -v cranelift/filetests/filetests/isa/interrupt-poll-after-call.clif (fails on base; passes with this patch).
Regression coverage: cranelift/filetests/filetests/isa/interrupt-poll-after-call.clif.

AI assistance: Codex helped implement and test this change. oss-scout independently replayed the regression before opening this PR.

:memo: cfallin submitted PR review:

Thanks. Can you address the comment below? Also, can you fix this for aarch64 as well?

:speech_balloon: cfallin created PR review comment:

Rather than doing this, let's do something else:

  • Let's not add any additional complexity to the MachBuffer; I think we can handle this during emission in the backends.
  • Let's keep some state in the EmitState recording the last offset at which we emitted a stack map.
  • Let's then add a NOP if and only if we try to emit a stack map at an offset that already has a stack map.
:cross_mark: cfallin closed without merge PR #15285.

cfallin commented on PR #15285:

@xixi-box I see this note in your latest commit message (ca9dda5):

Local Rust tests unavailable; validation pending CI.

Given the general principle of "contributors should be engaged with the project", and after talking with another maintainer and getting more context on some of your other PRs, I am going to go ahead and close this: you were asked to stop making AI-assisted contributions where you don't have a personal understanding of the work, and "have not even installed a Rust toolchain" is a good sign that you are not actually developing locally and understanding the issues here. (Also, a contributor pushing untested changes to our CI intentionally is wasteful.) I will fix this issue on my own in the manner I had suggested.

Thanks!
